source: Illinois Tech undergraduate catalog, catalog.iit.edu/courses (CS, MATH, and the Humanities and Social Sciences subjects), read October 2026. Descriptions are short paraphrases.

courses.title: Introduction to the Profession
courses.description: Introduces science and engineering as professions: how problems are solved and how solutions are judged against computational, financial, and social limits.

courses.description: Special projects. Needs instructor permission.

courses.description: Independent capstone project, which may include research, a literature review, data analysis, or an internship, guided by an advisor.

courses.title: Senior Capstone Project II
courses.description: Continues the independent capstone project, with set deliverables such as a thesis or poster.

courses.title: Integrative Psychology Seminar I
courses.description: Synthesis of issues and areas in psychology.
courses.prereqText: PSYC 203 or Graduate standing; requires 21 credit hours in psychology

courses.title: Integrative Psychology Seminar II
courses.description: Brings together key and current research and ideas on major issues in psychology.

courses.title: Undergraduate Psychology Seminar
courses.description: Reports and discussion of current problems and issues in psychology.

courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: Independent study that gathers and analyzes data on a significant problem. About 3 hours per week per credit.

courses.title: Advanced Research
courses.description: Advanced research for BSMP students.

courses.title: State and Local Government
courses.description: How federal, state, regional, and local governments relate: federalism theory, constitutional basis, courts, administration, and current debates.

courses.title: International Relations
courses.description: Major theories for understanding global issues such as war, peace, security, human rights, political economy, development, and international organizations.

courses.title: Democracy, Dictatorship, and Development
courses.description: Comparative political analysis, applied to instability, conflict, and transitions to stable democracy.

courses.title: American Foreign Policy
courses.description: How U.S. foreign policy is made, why it matters at home and abroad, and how its goals and carrying-out can be critiqued.

courses.title: American Government
courses.description: U.S. politics: how parties and interest groups link to institutions like the presidency and Congress, and how political culture shapes policy.

courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science
courses.description: Introductory course on a current topic announced by the instructor. Repeatable if the topic changes.

courses.title: Comparative Public Policy
courses.description: Why policies on welfare, health, education, and immigration differ across countries: culture, economics, institutions, and social organization.

courses.title: Chicago Politics
courses.description: Chicago's government past and present, with focus on the Democratic machine, its opponents, and the roles of class, ethnicity, race, and ideology.

courses.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
courses.description: How environmental policy is made and carried out from local to global levels, including conflicts over climate change, pollution, and conservation.

courses.title: Politics of Science and Technology
courses.description: Links among science, technology, and politics, including scientific advice to government and the social effects of technological change.

courses.title: Energy Policy
courses.description: Fossil fuel dependence and government efforts to conserve energy and develop alternatives, weighing economic, political, and environmental effects.

courses.title: Public Administration
courses.description: Administrative organization, decision-making, and structures, and the roles of government executives, fiscal procedures, and personnel management.

courses.title: Urban Policy
courses.description: Urban challenges such as economic change, fiscal strain, and marginalized groups, and how politicians and citizens respond. Also listed as SOC 354.

courses.title: Global Political Economy
courses.description: Economic, political, and cultural sides of globalization and international development.

courses.title: Government and Politics in Africa
courses.description: Current African politics in historical, economic, and cultural context, using country cases and regional issues.

courses.title: East Asian Political Economy
courses.description: Current East Asian politics in historical, economic, and cultural context, using country cases and regional issues.

courses.title: Topics in Political Science
courses.description: A current political science topic set by the instructor when scheduled.

courses.title: International Law and Organizations
courses.description: Global governance through political science and legal lenses, comparing frameworks such as those of the U.S., ICC, WTO, EU, and NAFTA.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Political Science
courses.description: Students choose a topic with a faculty member and finish an original, independent research project.

courses.title: Directed Readings in Political Science
courses.description: Independent reading and analysis on specific problems, supervised by a political science faculty member. Up to 3 credits.

courses.title: Microeconomics
courses.description: Models of firm and consumer behavior: supply and demand, market structures, efficiency, public goods, externalities, and game theory.

courses.title: Macroeconomics
courses.description: The AD-AS model, national income, growth, money, banking, and international economics, with focus on inflation, unemployment, and monetary and fiscal policy.

courses.title: Introduction to Economics
courses.description: Output, employment, and inflation, plus debates over fiscal and monetary policy, budget deficits, exchange rates, and trade deficits. Not open to business or economics majors or minors.

courses.title: Introduction to Econometrics
courses.description: Regression analysis theory and use, including panel data, instrumental variables, experiments, misspecification, nonlinear models, and big data.

courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
courses.description: Calculus-based models of price setting, consumer and producer theory, competitive and monopolistic markets, general equilibrium, and game theory.

courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
courses.description: Aggregate economic measurement and open-economy equilibrium, short- and long-run views of business cycles, growth, unemployment, and money, and policy options.
courses.prereqText: BUS 221 or (PSYC 203 and ECON 152) or ECON 211

courses.title: Business Economics
courses.description: Microeconomic analysis and industrial organization, market conditions and forces, and why governments step into and regulate markets.

courses.title: Sports Economics
courses.description: Budgeting and financing for teams, leagues, and venues, plus topics like esports, social media, and diversity, equity, and inclusion, with guest speakers and projects.

courses.title: Upper-Level Social Science
courses.description: An upper-level social science course. The catalog gives no further description.

courses.title: Upper-Level Social Science
courses.description: An upper-level social science course. The catalog gives no further description.

courses.title: Economics of Capital Investments
courses.description: Values capital projects in the public and private sectors with NPV, equivalent uniform benefit/cost, and IRR, with taxes, inflation, risk, and capital rationing. Business students may use it in place of BUS 351 with advisor approval.

courses.title: Social Psychology and Society
courses.description: Everyday judgments and their harmful social effects: the Fundamental Attribution Error, group influence, persuasion, brainwashing, helping behavior, and prejudice. Formerly SOC 308.

courses.title: Introduction to the Sociology of Space
courses.description: How space and spatial layouts shape people, social interaction, and community, up to city planning. Introduces basic sociological concepts and methods. Required for SOC 311.

courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.description: How society is structured and works, how individual behavior is analyzed, with emphasis on social problems.

courses.title: Introductory Special Topics in Sociology
courses.description: A currently relevant topic at an introductory level, announced by the instructor when scheduled. Repeatable if the topic differs.

courses.title: The Social Dimension of Science
courses.description: How social and psychological factors affect scientists' reasoning and behavior, set against the traditional view of science. Covers hype, resistance to discovery, controversy, competition, error, and fraud.

courses.title: Science and Belief
courses.description: Compares Western science with other belief systems, religion, and pseudo-science, and looks at cultural and ideological influences on scientific knowledge and public trust.

courses.title: Social Communication
courses.description: Verbal and nonverbal communication in personal, professional, and public life, and how to resolve misunderstandings. Covers interpersonal and group interaction, teamwork, leadership, and intercultural communication.

courses.title: Science in Society
courses.description: Science as an institution, its knowledge, and its practitioners in society, focused on how science shapes and is shaped by political, economic, and cultural contexts.

courses.title: Social Use of Space
courses.description: How people experience space and how spatial arrangements affect behavior. Compares planners' and users' ideas and argues for including users in spatial design.

courses.title: Deviant Behavior and Conformity
courses.description: How deviant behavior is defined, develops, and is controlled. Covers societal reactions and the patterns of deviance such as addiction, suicide, crime, and alcoholism.

courses.title: Technology and Social Change
courses.description: Social effects of new and cutting-edge technologies, with short- and long-term results seen through moral, ethical, socioeconomic, and educational views. Same as PS 362.

courses.title: Topics in Sociology
courses.description: A current sociology topic announced by the instructor when scheduled.

courses.title: Medical Sociology
courses.description: Sociological views of medicine, health, and illness: how social, economic, and political forces shape health ideas and medical science, including healthcare politics, inequality, medical technology, and the experience of illness.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Sociology
courses.description: Students pick a topic with a sociology faculty member, do research, and finish an original independent project.

courses.title: Directed Readings
courses.description: Independent reading or analysis on specific problems, supervised by a sociology faculty member. Up to 3 credits.

courses.title: Introduction to the Profession
courses.description: Social science careers and the skills professionals use in the field.

courses.title: States, Markets, and Society
courses.description: How governments, societies, and the global economy relate, including industrial change, technology, and welfare.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Policy
courses.description: Policy processes, mainly in the U.S. with some cross-country comparison, models, and policy-area analysis.

courses.title: Global Chicago
courses.description: How Chicago became a global city and what that did to government, business, education, nonprofits, and immigrants, with field trips.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Introductory course on a current topic. Repeatable if the topic differs.

courses.title: Introductory Special Topics in Social Sciences
courses.description: Introductory special topics course on a current social science subject, announced at scheduling.

courses.title: Social Science Research Methods
courses.description: Explanation in social science and qualitative and quantitative methods, including research design, measurement, surveys, and sampling.

courses.title: Social and Political Thought
courses.description: Major social and political theories on individuals and society, conflict, harmony, equality, and the state.

courses.title: Global Health
courses.description: Multidisciplinary overview of global health history, determinants, major diseases, governance, and health inequality.

courses.title: Social Inequality
courses.description: Social, economic, and political inequality in the U.S. and other societies, its causes, and its results.

courses.title: Problems of Multi-Ethnic, Multi-Religious States
courses.description: Political challenges, including conflict and fragmentation, in diverse societies in developed and developing countries.

courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Geographic data management, data models, basic spatial analysis, and GIS uses, through hands-on exercises.

courses.title: Criminal Justice Policy
courses.description: U.S. crime control policy, how social science informs it, and how inequality has shaped it.

courses.title: AI and Public Policy
courses.description: AI uses, regulation, and social results, through theory and case studies.

courses.title: Urban Policy
courses.description: City challenges such as fiscal stress, immigration, and marginalized groups, and how officials respond with policy.

courses.title: Regional Economic Development
courses.description: Why regions differ economically and how they respond to policy and economic change, using models and metrics.

courses.title: Race and Public Policy
courses.description: How racial inequality has shaped U.S. policy and the justice system in areas such as housing, education, and employment.

courses.title: Global Migration
courses.description: Migration history and current conditions across regions, including admission policies and immigrant integration.

courses.title: Innovation Policy
courses.description: Government efforts to promote innovation, including R&D roles, green R&D, patents, and international collaboration.

courses.title: International Development
courses.description: Multidisciplinary development theories, stakeholders, and issues like aid, sustainability, and migration, with policy evaluation.

courses.title: Computational Social Science
courses.description: Computational and agent-based models of inequality, conflict, and segregation. Students extend a model for research.

courses.title: Qualitative Social Science Research Methods
courses.description: Qualitative methods such as interviews, ethnography, and grounded theory, with applied workshops.

courses.title: Fieldwork Methods
courses.description: Work on a real-world project in the field.

courses.title: Methods of Economic Impact Analysis
courses.description: Input-output and social accounting methods to measure how environmental and social policy affects economies.

courses.title: Urban Planning Analysis
courses.description: Methods for gathering and judging empirical data to assess urban planning responses.

courses.title: Intermediate Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: GIS spatial modeling skills, including raster and vector models, map algebra, surface, and network analysis.
courses.prereqText: SSCI 225 or DS 151-261 or CS 104-201 or PSYC 203

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: An interdisciplinary current social science topic. Repeatable if the topic differs.

courses.title: Introduction to Survey Methodology
courses.description: Survey research design principles, including forming research questions and testable hypotheses.

courses.title: Program Evaluation
courses.description: Applied methods that public and nonprofit managers use to judge how well services are delivered.

courses.title: Directed UG Research
courses.description: Independent research project on the spatial spread of economic activity, with an instructor-approved topic.

courses.title: Social Sciences Colloquium
courses.description: Talks by invited scientists on social science research, to support academic and professional preparation.

courses.title: Public Service Internship
courses.description: A 120-hour internship at an approved organization that links classroom theory to practice.
